query_database.py:122 computes fence = max(3, 1 + longest backtick run in sql). Per CommonMark, a closing fence needs at least as many backticks as the opener and sits on a line with only backticks. Every run in the SQL is shorter than the fence, so no SQL line can close it. The info string 'sql' has no backticks, so the opener is valid. The SQL is placed between the fences on its own lines (line 123). Edge case: SQL with no backticks gives a 3-backtick fence, which is the normal case. I did not read the unit test.
